places.name: Mono Café
places.editorial: A bright, minimal corner café for specialty coffee, Japanese matcha and a quiet pause close to the creative heart of Poblenou.

places.name: El Tribut
places.editorial: A polished waterfront restaurant with a warm bohemian interior, Mediterranean cooking and views across Port Olímpic.

places.name: Les Filles
places.editorial: A serene, light-filled café with an elegant garden atmosphere in Gràcia.

places.name: Jaç Hi-Fi Café

places.name: Grand Hyatt Barcelona
places.editorial: A polished city hotel that welcomes dogs with beds, bowls and treats.

places.name: Onis Coffee
places.editorial: A beautifully restrained neighbourhood coffee bar with excellent espresso and pastries.

places.name: LOT Roasters
places.editorial: A bean-to-bar chocolate workshop and specialty coffee roastery focused on traceable Peruvian origins.

places.name: M.A.M.I. Café
places.editorial: An Italian-inspired specialty coffee bar in El Born, pairing coffee with DJ-set energy and a genuinely pet-friendly welcome - often led by Azul, the resident therapy Golden Retriever.

places.name: NOKKO
places.editorial: Specialty coffee, handmade pastries and rotating art on Enric Granados. A thoughtful little pause in the Eixample. Photo: NOKKO

places.name: Gresca
places.editorial: Seasonal small plates and a considered wine list on Provença, with an open kitchen and a quietly lively bar. Photo: Macarfi / This is Barcelona

places.name: SOMA
places.editorial: Mediterranean cooking with an Italian accent, seasonal dishes to share and a warm neighbourhood setting on Provença. Photo: SOMA Restaurant

places.name: BarBocata · Travessera
places.editorial: The original BarBocata on Travessera de Gràcia: generous sandwiches, tortilla and a relaxed bar for a long lunch. Photo: BarBocata

places.name: Morreig
places.editorial: Artisan pastries and house-made ice cream on Carrer de Verdi. French baking meets a playful take on dessert, from vanilla flan to brioche filled with ice cream. Images: Studio Ingrid Picanyol / Morreig.

places.name: Bárbara Bakery
places.editorial: Seasonal baking in Poblenou, from sourdough loaves and medialunas to lemon-and-cardamom babka. A good stop for something freshly baked after a neighbourhood walk. Photography: Bárbara Bakery.

places.name: Origo Bakery · Gràcia
places.editorial: Origo’s first bakery pairs organic sourdough and handmade pastries with specialty coffee. Its bread-led approach starts with regenerative farming. Photography: Origo Bakery · Gràcia.

places.name: La Papa · Aribau
places.editorial: Fresh daytime cooking and specialty coffee in a warm, design-led Eixample café. The handmade ceramics are part of La Papa’s own collection. Photography: La Papa · Aribau.

places.name: Wanna Place
places.editorial: A small Sant Gervasi café for specialty coffee and a pastry break, tucked into a neighbourhood corner close to Plaça de Sant Joaquim. Photography: Vannelle Canille / Vannelle Walks.

places.name: Otsu
places.editorial: A Japanese-inspired Poblenou café for egg sandos, seasonal breakfasts and lunch. Coffee and pastries continue after the kitchen closes. Photography: Paulina Rodriguez / Otsu.

places.name: Café Schallert
places.editorial: Austrian baking at Hotel Brummell: house-made strudel, Sachertorte and Three Marks coffee. Stay for a slow breakfast in the plant-filled atrium. Photography: Žiga Mihelčič and Maria Astrand / Café Schallert.

places.name: Berbena
places.editorial: A compact restaurant on Carrer de Minerva, built around seasonal plates, house-made sourdough and a thoughtful wine list. An intimate stop for a longer meal. Photography: Berbena.

places.name: Jon Cake & Coffee
places.editorial: Jon García’s cheese-led cakes meet specialty coffee in the Born. Choose a slice of the signature cheesecake or one of the changing varieties. Photography: Jon Cake & Coffee.

places.name: Casa Camper Barcelona
places.editorial: A design hotel in the Raval, close to the MACBA, with relaxed shared spaces and a rooftop terrace. A central base for exploring the old city. Contact the hotel before booking to confirm current pet-stay conditions and any fees. Photography: Casa Camper Barcelona.

places.name: Casa Bonay
places.editorial: A restored 19th-century house on Gran Via with tiled floors, courtyard rooms and lively food-and-drink spaces. A characterful Eixample base for a city stay. Pet-friendly stays are available. Confirm the room arrangements with the hotel before booking. Photography: Casa Bonay.

places.name: Bodega Bonay
places.editorial: Seasonal Mediterranean plates and a considered wine list inside Casa Bonay. A low-key place to settle into an unhurried meal on Gran Via. Dogs are welcome; confirm the seating arrangements with the team. Photography: Bodega Bonay.

places.name: Bar La Camila
places.editorial: An old-style Gràcia neighbourhood bar with specialty coffee, tortilla and small plates. Come for breakfast or linger over a vermouth later in the day. Dogs are welcome; confirm the seating arrangements with the team. Photography: Andreu Font / In and Out Barcelona.

places.name: Benzina
places.editorial: Italian cooking and cocktails on Passatge de Pere Calders. Come for pasta, including its signature carbonara, in a relaxed Sant Antoni setting. Photography: Benzina.

places.name: Balzac Barcelona
places.editorial: A specialty-coffee stop on Passeig de Sant Joan, pairing carefully made coffee with pastries. A simple pause along one of the city’s best walking streets. Dogs are welcome inside. Photography: Time Out Barcelona.

places.name: Honest Greens · Pedralbes Centre
places.editorial: Vegetable-led market plates and seasonal salads at Pedralbes Centre. An easy, informal stop for a fresh lunch in Les Corts. Dogs are welcome; confirm the seating arrangements with the team. Photography: Honest Greens · Pedralbes Centre.

places.name: Corgi Café · Arc de Triomf
places.editorial: Specialty coffee, all-day brunch and resident corgis on Carrer del Comerç. Stop for pancakes before a stroll towards the Arc de Triomf. Dogs are welcome inside on a lead, provided they are comfortable around other dogs. Water is available. The café asks visitors to respect its resident corgis’ rest. Photography: Corgi Café · Arc de Triomf.

places.name: Koke
places.editorial: A dog grooming studio and concept store in Poblenou, with daycare, carefully chosen walking accessories and a café corner while your dog is pampered. Dog grooming and daycare are available by appointment. Ask the team about the right service for your dog. Photography: Koke.

places.name: Fochiko
places.editorial: A boutique dog grooming salon beside Turó Park, with hand-scissored styling, coat treatments and baths tailored to each dog. Dog grooming is offered for small, medium, large and giant dogs. Book a session with the salon. Photography: Fochiko.

places.name: Breto
places.editorial: A Poblenou concept store devoted to dogs, with natural food, considered accessories and grooming. Browse walking gear and everyday essentials in a warm, pared-back space. A dog concept store with grooming services; contact the team for appointments. Photography: Mandai Design / Breto.

places.name: Soi & Co
places.editorial: A calm, design-led soy café for matcha, vegan desserts and slow afternoons together.

places.name: Sofi Bakery
places.editorial: A low-intervention neighbourhood bakery devoted to organic grains, slow fermentation and beautifully made bread.

places.name: Zacharias
places.editorial: An intentional specialty coffee bar with a nostalgic soul, precise pours and a calm, considered interior.

places.name: Annelies
places.editorial: A bright neighbourhood breakfast spot known for creative seasonal plates, thoughtful coffee and relaxed mornings.

places.name: Two Trick Pony
places.editorial: A warm, easy-going brunch room serving generous breakfasts and coffee - with dogs explicitly welcome.

places.name: Open House
places.editorial: A neighbourhood café and community space for house-baked sourdough, sweets, full brunch and unhurried company.

places.name: Goodlyfe
places.editorial: A relaxed riverside café by the East Side Gallery for specialty coffee, matcha, small bites and sunny outdoor pauses.

places.name: Riviera
places.editorial: A recommended Copenhagen stop from The Dog Friendly Guide collection.

places.name: Lokal
places.editorial: A Vesterbro coffee stop on Sønder Boulevard, with art and vintage design alongside the espresso. An easy pause on a walk through the neighbourhood. Dogs are welcome inside.

places.name: Apotek 57
places.editorial: In the former pharmacy that houses the FRAMA Studio Store, this Nyboder café pairs seasonal plates and pastries with warm timber and shelves of ceramics. Dogs are welcome. Ask the café about seating if you plan to stay. Photography: FRAMA

places.name: La Cabra · Nordhavn
places.editorial: La Cabra’s harbour-side roastery and café pairs carefully brewed coffee with a brick-lined room. Make it a stop on a walk through Nordhavn’s old port streets. Dogs are welcome at this Nordhavn location. Ask the café about seating. Photography: La Cabra

places.name: The Roe Bar
places.editorial: The café inside Louise Roe Gallery pairs breakfast and seasonal lunch with coffee and pastries. Its sculptural tables and long counter make it an inviting pause in the city centre. Dogs are welcome inside. Photography: LOUISE ROE

places.name: Lille Fugl
places.shortDescription: Bakery café & wine bar · Indre By
places.editorial: Tucked beneath the Gammel Strand art centre, this little café from the Flere Fugle team is a stop for baked goods, breakfast and a glass of wine later in the day. Dogs are welcome at Lille Fugl. Ask the café about seating. Photography: Flere Fugle

places.name: Beau Marché
places.shortDescription: French café & wine bar · Indre By
places.editorial: Past the design shop on Ny Østergade, this French café and wine bar serves classics such as croque monsieur and omelettes. The little courtyard is a quiet place to pause in the city centre. Dogs are welcome. Ask the café whether indoor seating is available. Photography: VisitCopenhagen

places.name: Prolog Coffee · Paper Island
places.editorial: Prolog’s Paper Island coffee bar sits on the harbour in Christianshavn. Stop for espresso or filter coffee from the Copenhagen roaster before a walk along the waterfront. Dogs are welcome inside at Paper Island and at all Prolog coffee bars. Photography: Prolog Coffee

places.name: Amator
places.editorial: An intimate Østerbro restaurant where omelettes take centre stage. Long oak tables and a compact open kitchen give breakfast or lunch the feel of a meal at someone’s home. Dogs are welcome. Ask the restaurant about seating. Photography: Paolo Galgani

places.name: Bottega Barlie
places.editorial: A neighbourhood restaurant on Fredericiagade, equally suited to a slow breakfast or a seasonal dinner and a glass of wine. The menu shifts with what is in season. Dogs are welcome. Ask the restaurant about seating. Photography: Bottega Barlie

places.name: Zoku Copenhagen
places.editorial: An Amager aparthotel with compact lofts, full kitchens and rooftop social spaces. A practical base for a longer stay or a weekend with your dog. One dog up to 20 kg per loft. A cleaning fee applies. Dogs can join you in most social spaces, with the Living Kitchen restaurant excluded. Hotel pet policy Photography: Zoku Copenhagen

places.name: Gotcha Matcha
places.editorial: A soft-toned matcha café in Eppendorf, with curved seating, Japanese tea and room for a quiet pause together.

places.name: Marshall Street Coffee
places.editorial: An Australian-inspired café in the old town for specialty coffee, generous breakfasts and something freshly baked.

places.name: Pet Shop Boyz
places.editorial: A dog concept store on Mittelweg bringing together thoughtful accessories, treats and everyday essentials for dogs and their people.

places.name: SCADI · living with dogs
places.editorial: A considered selection of beds, bowls and walking accessories in Winterhude, with an eye for pieces that feel at home in everyday life.

places.name: Heimat Restaurant
places.editorial: The warm dining room at 25hours Hotel HafenCity, serving familiar dishes from Germany, Austria and Switzerland beside the harbour.

places.name: Klear Labs
places.shortDescription: Bakery & specialty coffee · West London · Golborne Road
places.editorial: A quiet neighbourhood bakery and coffee stop, selected for its considered interiors and easy pace.

places.name: % Arabica
places.shortDescription: Specialty coffee · East London · Broadway Market
places.editorial: A minimal Japanese coffee bar with beans roasted in-house and a small terrace at the heart of East London.

places.name: Abuelo
places.editorial: A warm Australian–South American café for thoughtful coffee, colourful brunch plates and an unhurried city pause. Well-behaved dogs are welcome, with no other restrictions specified by the team. Photography: @abuelocafeuk

places.name: Workshop Coffee
places.editorial: A light-filled café and coffee academy serving seasonal single origins, an all-day menu and evening aperitivo. Dogs are welcome. Photography: @workshopcoffee

places.name: WOLFOX Savoy London
places.editorial: A grand café just off the Strand, with pale walls, generous windows and speciality coffee. Come for a slow breakfast before a walk along the river. Well-behaved dogs welcome. Photography: @wolfoxsavoylondon, used with permission.

places.name: Nagare Coffee · Soho
places.editorial: A quiet coffee stop on Newburgh Street, just off Carnaby, with a pale storefront, carefully chosen beans and a Japanese approach to brewing. Hosts dog portrait sessions with Dogs by Jeff.

places.name: The Laslett
places.editorial: A quiet Notting Hill base across five Victorian townhouses, with art-filled rooms, books and a neighbourhood bar. A considered city stay moments from Notting Hill Gate. Dogs welcome. Contact the hotel before booking for the applicable pet terms. Photography: @thelaslett, used with permission.

places.name: WatchHouse Fitzrovia
places.editorial: Dark oak booths, stainless steel counters and carefully made coffee in an understated Fitzrovia space, with brunch and fresh bakes. Dog-friendly, as listed by WatchHouse.

places.name: Bow Wow London
places.shortDescription: Dog shop · Central London · Covent Garden
places.editorial: A Seven Dials boutique with considered accessories, toys and treats, alongside a dedicated grooming salon.

places.name: Love My Human
places.editorial: The King’s Road boutique brings together beautifully made dog accessories, beds, toys and grooming essentials.

places.name: Dogeast
places.editorial: An independent pet shop and grooming studio in London Dock, with a curated selection of food, treats and toys.

places.name: Big City Dog
places.editorial: A Kensington concept store combining dog accessories and treats with grooming, a self-wash station and an in-house matcha bar.

places.name: Mello World
places.editorial: A Walton Street boutique for dogs and their people, close to Knightsbridge and Chelsea.

places.name: George’s Dog Boutique
places.shortDescription: Dog shop · South London · Wimbledon Village
places.editorial: A Wimbledon Village boutique for thoughtful walkwear, dog beds and accessories, with dogs welcome to try on their favourites.

places.name: Yeni
places.editorial: A seasonal Turkish restaurant on Beak Street, where chef Civan Er brings Anatolian flavours and open-fire cooking to Soho. Dogs are welcome. Photography: @yenisoho

places.name: Granger & Co · Marylebone
places.editorial: An Australian-inspired neighbourhood restaurant for breakfast, lunch and dinner, with a warm dining room on Marylebone High Street. Small, well-behaved dogs are welcome. Keep them on a lead, on the floor and close to you. Photography: @grangerandco

places.name: Studio Coffee
places.editorial: A vinyl-led coffee shop and cocktail bar on Bedford Street, pairing coffee and pastries with a soundtrack that invites you to stay awhile. Dogs are welcome. Photography: @studiocoffee__

places.name: Paradox Design + Coffee
places.editorial: A small coffee and design space in Netil Market, with a changing selection of beans and a personal, creative approach to the everyday coffee stop. Dogs are welcome. Photography: @paradox_design_coffee

places.name: Leigh’s
places.editorial: A neighbourhood coffee stop in De Beauvoir for cakes, toasties and seasonal drinks, with a busy counter and a warm welcome for local dogs. Dogs are welcome. Please keep reactive dogs on a lead. Photography: @leighslondon

places.name: Estate Office Coffee
places.editorial: A local coffee shop on Greyhound Lane for coffee and sourdough toasties, with a Polaroid wall celebrating its four-legged regulars. Dogs are welcome. Photography: @estateofficecoffee

places.name: Canteen
places.editorial: A walk-in neighbourhood restaurant on Portobello Road, with a changing menu and tables for a leisurely lunch or evening meal. Dogs are welcome. Photography: @canteen.310

places.name: EVE Kensington
places.editorial: A richly coloured café at Ember Locke, with pastries, coffee and a relaxed setting for a Kensington pause. Dogs are welcome. Photography: @evekensington

places.name: Scenery
places.editorial: A coffee roastery and café at Jerwood Space, with a glass-roofed courtyard, coffee roasted on site and a kitchen serving breakfast, lunch and Saturday brunch. Dogs are welcome on a lead. Water bowls and complimentary dog treats are available. Photography: @scenerycoffeeroasters

places.name: Paper & Cup
places.shortDescription: Vintage & takeaway coffee · East London · Shoreditch
places.editorial: A community-minded stop on Calvert Avenue, now focused on vintage and second-hand clothing, with specialty coffee to take away. Purchases support Spitalfields Crypt Trust. Dogs are welcome. Primarily a second-hand clothing shop with takeaway coffee. Photography: @paperandcupshoreditch

places.name: Ozone Coffee · Shoreditch
places.editorial: A Leonard Street coffee stop for espresso, rotating filter coffees and seasonal breakfast or lunch, just around the corner from Old Street. Dogs are welcome at all Ozone cafés. Photography: @ozonecoffeeuk

places.name: Qima Café · Fitzrovia
places.editorial: A Fitzrovia café pairing carefully sourced coffee with pâtisserie and brunch. Its tree-to-cup approach connects the coffee served here with the farmers behind it. Dogs are welcome at both Qima cafés, with no restrictions or additional fees. Photography: @qima.cafe

places.name: Hermanas Arce

places.name: Kanso Coffee Lab
places.editorial: A quiet courtyard coffee lab in the Residenzpassage, with a pared-back interior and a considered approach to espresso and filter coffee. Confirm current dog access directly with the café before visiting. Photography: Kanso Coffee Lab.

places.name: Man Versus Machine · Glockenbach
places.editorial: The original Man Versus Machine coffee shop on Müllerstraße, serving specialty espresso, filter coffee, matcha and Franzbrötchen in the heart of Glockenbachviertel. Confirm current dog access directly with the café before visiting. Photography: Man Versus Machine.

places.name: The Spirited Goat
places.editorial: A neighbourhood coffee and matcha bar on Hohenzollernstraße, with beans from European roasteries and carefully sourced teas. Stop for an espresso or a slow filter coffee in Schwabing. Dogs are welcome, confirmed directly by the café. Photography: The Spirited Goat.

places.name: Schwarzreiter Tagesbar
places.shortDescription: Bavarian à la carte restaurant · Altstadt-Lehel
places.editorial: The relaxed à la carte dining room at Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten Kempinski on Maximilianstraße, serving seasonal Bavarian cooking from lunch into the evening. Dogs are welcome in the Tagesbar, confirmed directly by the team. The separate Schwarzreiter fine-dining restaurant does not admit dogs. Photography: Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten Kempinski Munich.

places.name: Das METTA
places.editorial: A plant-filled café and organic bakery on Barer Straße, with vegan, gluten-free bakes and coffee in a relaxed community space. Make it a pastry stop while exploring Maxvorstadt. Confirm current dog access with the café before visiting. Photography: Das METTA.

places.name: Filou Coffee
places.editorial: Coffee from Filou’s own roastery, ceremonial matcha and a changing selection of breakfast bites on Augustenstraße. The café also brings local dog people together for coffee walks. Confirm current dog access with the team before visiting. Photography: Filou Coffee.

places.name: Schwan Locke
places.editorial: Colourful studios with kitchens, a leafy courtyard and shared spaces for settling into Munich at your own pace. Theresienwiese is a short walk away. The hotel welcomes dogs; check pet-room availability and the current conditions when booking. Photography: Locke.

Continue towards Rue des Martyrs for a second coffee or something baked.

Finish with a relaxed late breakfast or lunch nearby.

Continue to a dog café and boutique made around life together.
Close the afternoon with an early table in the heart of Le Marais.
